## R18 — who owns the processors

- `PatchcoreModel.__init__(self, layers: collections.abc.Sequence[str], backbone: str = 'wide_resnet50_2', pre_trained: bool = True, num_neighbors: int = 9) -> None`
- Lightning `Patchcore.__init__(self, backbone: str = 'wide_resnet50_2', layers: collections.abc.Sequence[str] = ('layer2', 'layer3'), pre_trained: bool = True, coreset_sampling_ratio: float = 0.1, num_neighbors: int = 9, precision: str | anomalib.PrecisionType = <PrecisionType.FLOAT32: 'float32'>, pre_processor: torch.nn.modules.module.Module | bool = True, post_processor: torch.nn.modules.module.Module | bool = True, evaluator: anomalib.metrics.evaluator.Evaluator | bool = True, visualizer: anomalib.visualization.base.Visualizer | bool = True) -> None`

Conclusion: `pre_processor` / `post_processor` are accepted by the Lightning wrapper `Patchcore`, not by the torch `PatchcoreModel` — using the torch model directly avoids them, as the design assumed.
